docs.title: AI Codebase Knowledge Builder
docs.text: Ever stared at a new codebase written by others feeling completely lost? This project analyzes GitHub repositories and creates beginner-friendly tutorials explaining exactly how the code works - all powered by AI! Our intelligent system automatically breaks down complex codebases into digestible explanations that even beginners can understand.

docs.title: 🚀 Getting Started
docs.text:
1. Clone this repository 

    git clone https://github.com/ardennguyen/Codebase-Knowledge-Builder

  2. Install dependencies (we highly recommend using a virtual environment of your choice like venv, conda, uv, or pyenv to avoid polluting your global system): 

    pip install -r requirements.txt

  3. Set up LLM in utils/call_llm.py by providing credentials via a .env file. You can use native Gemini by setting GEMINI_API_KEY. For OpenRouter, set LLM_PROVIDER=OPENROUTER and OPENROUTER_API_KEY.

  4. Generate a complete codebase tutorial by running the main script: 

    # Analyze a GitHub repository
python main.py --repo https://github.com/username/repo --include "*.py" "*.js" --exclude "tests/*" --max-size 50000

# Or, analyze a local directory
python main.py --dir /path/to/your/codebase --include "*.py" --exclude "*test*"

# Or, generate a tutorial in Vietnamese
python main.py --repo https://github.com/username/repo --language "Vietnamese"

docs.title: CLI Options
docs.text:
• --repo or --dir - Specify either a GitHub repo URL or a local directory path (required, mutually exclusive)
  • -n, --name - Project name (optional, derived from URL/directory if omitted)
  • -t, --token - GitHub token (or set GITHUB_TOKEN environment variable)
  • -o, --output - Output directory (default: ./output)
  • -i, --include - Files to include (e.g., *.py *.js). Defaults to * (all files).
  • -e, --exclude - Files to exclude. Custom patterns are automatically merged with a massive global exclusion list (build caches, node_modules, binaries, media, AI environments) AND your repository's native .gitignore rules.
  • -s, --max-size - Maximum file size in bytes (default: 200KB)
  • --language - Language for the generated tutorial (default: "english")
  • --max-abstractions - Maximum number of abstractions to identify (default: 10)
  • --no-cache - Disable LLM response caching (default: caching enabled)
  • --thinking-level - Thinking effort level for native Gemini, OpenRouter, and Ollama reasoning models (e.g., low, medium, high). Leave empty to use model defaults.
  • --max-tokens - Maximum number of tokens for the context window (default: fetched dynamically from the model).
  • --mode - Documentation style (tutorial, advanced, api-reference, sdk). (default: tutorial)
  • --advanced - Legacy flag: equivalent to --mode advanced
  • --mkdocs - Format output for MkDocs Material (adds YAML frontmatter & nav snippet)
  • --incremental - Enable MD5 incremental caching to skip unchanged modules (Only supported in --mode api-reference)
  • --force-rebuild - Clear incremental cache and regenerate all chapters from scratch (use with --incremental)
  • --batch - Maximum files per batch when using map-reduce mode (default: 50).
  • --force-batch - Force the pipeline to use map-reduce mode regardless of context limits.
  • --debug - Enable verbose debug output.
  • --cleanup - Clean up logs and cache JSON at the end of the script (default: No).

The application will crawl the repository, analyze the codebase structure, generate tutorial content in the specified language, and save the output in the specified directory (default: ./output). This includes individual chapter files, an index.md, and a compiled full_content.md containing the complete tutorial with a Table of Contents.

Built using Pocket Flow, a 100-line LLM framework.

docs.title: 1. Requirements
docs.text:
Notes for AI: Keep it simple and clear. If the requirements are abstract, write concrete user stories

User Story: As a developer onboarding to a new codebase, I want a tutorial automatically generated from its GitHub repository or local directory, optionally in a specific language. The system supports four documentation styles: a tutorial mode that explains core abstractions with beginner-friendly language, analogies, and code walkthroughs; an advanced mode that produces architecture deep-dives aimed at senior developers or PMs joining a project mid-way, covering design patterns, key dependencies, and practical onboarding notes; an api-reference mode that generates exhaustive, formal API documentation for every code module (1:1 file-to-chapter mapping); and an sdk mode that produces SDK-style integration guides. The system must also gracefully handle codebases of any size by dynamically switching to a Map-Reduce approach when context limits are reached.

Input: - A publicly accessible GitHub repository URL or a local directory path. - A project name (optional, will be derived from the URL/directory if not provided). - Desired language for the tutorial (optional, defaults to English). - Advanced configurations: documentation style (--mode), token scaling (--max-tokens, --batch, --force-batch), prompting (--thinking-level, --max-abstractions), caching (--no-cache), output format (--mkdocs, --incremental), debugging (--debug), and execution cleanup (--cleanup).

Output: - A directory named after the project containing: - An index.md file with: - A high-level project summary (potentially translated). - A Mermaid flowchart diagram visualizing relationships between abstractions (using potentially translated names/labels). - An ordered list of links to chapter files (using potentially translated names). - A link to full_content.md at the bottom. - Individual Markdown files for each chapter (01_chapter_one.md, 02_chapter_two.md, etc.) detailing core abstractions in a logical order (potentially translated content). - A full_content.md (inside the project subdirectory) containing all merged chapters and a Table of Contents. - When --mkdocs is used: YAML frontmatter is injected into every chapter, filenames mirror source directory structure instead of numbered prefixes, and a nav_snippet.yml navigation file is generated for MkDocs integration. - When --incremental is used (api-reference mode only): a .doc_cache_manifest.json tracks MD5 hashes of source files to skip regeneration of unchanged modules across runs.

docs.title: 2. Flow Design
docs.text: Notes for AI: 1. Consider the design patterns of agent, map-reduce, rag, and workflow. Apply them if they fit. 2. Present a concise, high-level description of the workflow.

docs.title: Applicable Design Pattern:
docs.text:
This project primarily uses a Workflow pattern with dynamic branching into a Map-Reduce pattern. The chapter writing step also utilizes a BatchNode.

  1. Workflow & Routing: The overall process fetches code, estimates token payloads, and routes based on context limits. If the codebase fits the LLM window, it goes directly to abstraction identification.
  2. Map-Reduce: If the codebase exceeds context limits (or if forced), the codebase is grouped into token-aware, directory-isolated batches (each batch stays under the effective token limit and never mixes files from different directories). A MapAbstractions BatchNode processes each batch individually, and a ReduceAbstractions Node merges them into a global list.
  3. Batch Processing: The WriteChapters node processes each identified abstraction independently (map) before final tutorial compilation.

docs.title: Flow high-level Design:
docs.text:
1. FetchRepo: Crawls the specified repository/directory using crawl_github_files or crawl_local_files.
  2. ContextRouter: Analyzes the total token payload of the fetched files using tiktoken. Dynamically calculates prompt overhead (template tokens + directory tree tokens) and computes an effective limit = safety_limit - prompt_overhead. If --mode api-reference is used, routes to "deterministic". If the file content tokens exceed this effective limit or if --force-batch is used, it chunks files into token-aware, directory-isolated batches (never mixing files from different directories) and routes to "batch". Also builds a compact directory tree of all files (stored in shared["directory_tree"]) for cross-batch awareness. With --debug, displays detailed per-batch file lists and token breakdowns. Otherwise, it routes to "direct".
  3. Path A: Direct
    • IdentifyAbstractions: Analyzes the entire codebase at once to identify core abstractions.
  4. Path B: Map-Reduce
    • MapAbstractions (BatchNode): Analyzes each localized directory chunk to extract partial abstractions. Each batch receives the full directory tree for cross-batch awareness.
    • ReduceAbstractions: Merges overlapping/partial abstractions into a global list of architecture components.
  5. Path C: Deterministic (api-reference mode)
    • DeterministicFileMapper: Bypasses LLM-based abstraction discovery entirely. Uses a lightweight LLM call to filter out non-code files (configs, UI layouts, static assets), then creates a 1:1 mapping of each code file to a documentation module. Skips AnalyzeRelationships and OrderChapters, routing directly to WriteChapters.
  6. AnalyzeRelationships (Paths A & B only): Takes the unified abstractions list (from either path) and generates a high-level project summary and relationships diagram. Uses token-budget-aware file inclusion: the budget is split evenly across abstractions, with unused budget redistributed in a second pass, maximizing code context without exceeding the context window.
  7. OrderChapters (Paths A & B only): Determines the most logical sequence to present the abstractions.
  8. WriteChapters (BatchNode): Iterates through the ordered abstractions and writes detailed Markdown chapters using context-aware code inclusion.
  9. CombineTutorial: Assembles the final outputs including index.md, individual chapter files, and a compiled full_content.md.
flowchart TD
    A[FetchRepo] --> Router[ContextRouter]

    Router -->|direct| B[IdentifyAbstractions]
    Router -->|batch| M1[MapAbstractions]
    Router -->|deterministic| DFM[DeterministicFileMapper]
    M1 --> M2[ReduceAbstractions]

    B --> C[AnalyzeRelationships]
    M2 --> C

    C --> D[OrderChapters]
    D --> E[Batch WriteChapters]
    DFM --> E
    E --> F[CombineTutorial]

def crawl_local_files(directory, include_patterns=None, exclude_patterns=None,
                      max_file_size=None, use_relative_paths=True) -> dict:
    # Returns: {"files": {relative_path_str: content_str, ...}}

Directory Pruning Algorithm (critical for nested directories like Core.User/.vs/): 

# During os.walk, for each subdirectory d:
excluded_dirs = set()
for d in dirs:
    dirpath_rel = os.path.relpath(os.path.join(root, d), directory)
    # Check .gitignore first
    if gitignore_spec and gitignore_spec.match_file(dirpath_rel):
        excluded_dirs.add(d)
        continue
    # Check exclude patterns — strip trailing /* for directory matching
    if exclude_patterns:
        for pattern in exclude_patterns:
            dir_pattern = pattern[:-2] if pattern.endswith("/*") else pattern
            if fnmatch.fnmatch(dirpath_rel, dir_pattern) or fnmatch.fnmatch(d, dir_pattern):
                excluded_dirs.add(d)
                break
# Remove matched dirs to prevent os.walk descent
for d in dirs.copy():
    if d in excluded_dirs:
        dirs.remove(d)

Note: Directory validation: raises ValueError if directory path doesn't exist. Loads .gitignore with utf-8-sig encoding (BOM-safe). All directories and files are sorted() for deterministic traversal order.

Progress Display Format: - Green (\033[92m): [processed] — Successfully read files - Gray (\033[90m): [excluded (.gitignore)] / [excluded (not in include list)] — Skipped by pattern - Red (\033[91m): [size limit: {size_kb:.0f}KB] — Exceeded max_file_size - Red (\033[91m): [cannot process: not a text file] / [cannot process: {e}] — Binary/encoding errors

Note: After crawling, prints a --- Crawl Summary --- block with total found, processed, excluded, size limited, and non-text counts.

Triggered when repo_url.startswith("git@") or repo_url.endswith(".git"): 

with tempfile.TemporaryDirectory() as tmpdirname:
    print(f"Cloning SSH repo {repo_url} to temp dir {tmpdirname} ...")
    try:
        repo = git.Repo.clone_from(repo_url, tmpdirname)
    except Exception as e:
        print(f"Error cloning repo: {e}")
        return {"files": {}, "stats": {"error": str(e)}}

    files = {}
    skipped_files = []

    # --- ANSI colors ---
    C_GREEN  = "\033[92m"
    C_GRAY   = "\033[90m"
    C_RED    = "\033[91m"
    C_RESET  = "\033[0m"

    # --- Counters ---
    count_processed = 0
    count_excluded = 0
    count_size_limit = 0
    count_non_text = 0
    skipped_size_list = []
    skipped_non_text_list = []
    entry_num = 0

    # --- Load .gitignore (BOM-safe) ---
    gitignore_path = os.path.join(tmpdirname, ".gitignore")
    gitignore_spec = None
    if os.path.exists(gitignore_path):
        try:
            with open(gitignore_path, "r", encoding="utf-8-sig") as f:
                gitignore_spec = pathspec.PathSpec.from_lines("gitwildmatch", f.readlines())
        except Exception:
            pass

    for root, dirs, filenames in os.walk(tmpdirname):
        # --- Directory pruning (same algorithm as crawl_local_files) ---
        excluded_dirs = set()
        for d in sorted(dirs):
            dirpath_rel = os.path.relpath(os.path.join(root, d), tmpdirname)
            reason = None
            if gitignore_spec and gitignore_spec.match_file(dirpath_rel):
                reason = "excluded (.gitignore)"
            elif exclude_patterns:
                for pattern in exclude_patterns:
                    dir_pattern = pattern[:-2] if pattern.endswith("/*") else pattern
                    if fnmatch.fnmatch(dirpath_rel, dir_pattern) or fnmatch.fnmatch(d, dir_pattern):
                        reason = "excluded"
                        break
            if reason:
                excluded_dirs.add(d)
                entry_num += 1
                count_excluded += 1
                print(f"{C_GRAY}  [{entry_num}] {dirpath_rel}/ [{reason}]{C_RESET}")

        for d in dirs.copy():
            if d in excluded_dirs:
                dirs.remove(d)
        dirs.sort()  # Deterministic traversal order

        # --- File processing ---
        for filename in sorted(filenames):
            abs_path = os.path.join(root, filename)
            rel_path = os.path.relpath(abs_path, tmpdirname)
            entry_num += 1

            if not should_include_file(rel_path, filename, gitignore_spec=gitignore_spec):
                count_excluded += 1
                print(f"{C_GRAY}  [{entry_num}] {rel_path} [excluded]{C_RESET}")
                continue

            try:
                file_size = os.path.getsize(abs_path)
            except OSError:
                continue

            if file_size > max_file_size:
                count_size_limit += 1
                skipped_size_list.append(rel_path)
                size_kb = file_size / 1024
                print(f"{C_RED}  [{entry_num}] {rel_path} [size limit: {size_kb:.0f}KB]{C_RESET}")
                continue

            try:
                with open(abs_path, "r", encoding="utf-8-sig") as f:
                    content = f.read()
                files[rel_path] = content
                count_processed += 1
                print(f"{C_GREEN}  [{entry_num}] {rel_path} [processed]{C_RESET}")
            except (UnicodeDecodeError, ValueError):
                count_non_text += 1
                skipped_non_text_list.append(rel_path)
                print(f"{C_RED}  [{entry_num}] {rel_path} [cannot process: not a text file]{C_RESET}")
            except Exception as e:
                count_non_text += 1
                skipped_non_text_list.append(rel_path)
                print(f"{C_RED}  [{entry_num}] {rel_path} [cannot process: {e}]{C_RESET}")

    # --- Crawl Summary ---
    total_fetched = count_processed + count_excluded + count_size_limit + count_non_text
    print(f"\n--- Crawl Summary ---")
    print(f"  Total found : {total_fetched}")
    print(f"{C_GREEN}  Processed   : {count_processed}{C_RESET}")
    if count_excluded > 0:
        print(f"{C_GRAY}  Excluded    : {count_excluded}{C_RESET}")
    if count_size_limit > 0:
        print(f"{C_RED}  Size limit  : {count_size_limit}{C_RESET}")
        for sf in skipped_size_list:
            print(f"{C_RED}    - {sf}{C_RESET}")
    if count_non_text > 0:
        print(f"{C_RED}  Non-text    : {count_non_text}{C_RESET}")
        for sf in skipped_non_text_list:
            print(f"{C_RED}    - {sf}{C_RESET}")
    print(f"---------------------")

    return {
        "files": files,
        "stats": {
            "downloaded_count": len(files),
            "skipped_count": len(skipped_files),
            "skipped_files": skipped_files,
            "base_path": None,
            "include_patterns": include_patterns,
            "exclude_patterns": exclude_patterns,
            "source": "ssh_clone"
        }
    }

parsed_url = urlparse(repo_url)
path_parts = parsed_url.path.strip('/').split('/')
owner, repo = path_parts[0], path_parts[1]

headers = {"Accept": "application/vnd.github.v3+json"}

Step 2 — Dynamic Branch Detection (handles multi-segment branch names like feature/foo): 

if len(path_parts) > 2 and 'tree' == path_parts[2]:
    join_parts = lambda i: '/'.join(path_parts[i:])

    # Fetch all branches
    branches = fetch_branches(owner, repo)  # GET /repos/{owner}/{repo}/branches
    branch_names = map(lambda b: b.get("name"), branches)

    # Match URL path against branch names (handles multi-segment names)
    relevant_path = join_parts(3)
    ref = next((name for name in branch_names if relevant_path.startswith(name)), None)

    # Fallback: check if it's a commit/tree hash
    if ref is None:
        tree = path_parts[3]
        ref = tree if check_tree(owner, repo, tree) else None  # GET /repos/{owner}/{repo}/git/trees/{tree}

    # Extract subdirectory (accounts for multi-slash branch names)
    part_index = 5 if '/' in ref else 4
    specific_path = join_parts(part_index) if part_index < len(path_parts) else ""
else:
    ref = None  # Let GitHub use default branch
    specific_path = ""

Step 3 — Remote .gitignore Fetch: 

gi_url = f"https://api.github.com/repos/{owner}/{repo}/contents/.gitignore"
gi_params = {"ref": ref} if ref is not None else {}
gi_resp = requests.get(gi_url, headers=headers, params=gi_params, timeout=(10, 10))
if gi_resp.status_code == 200:
    gi_data = gi_resp.json()
    if "content" in gi_data and gi_data.get("encoding") == "base64":
        gi_content = base64.b64decode(gi_data["content"]).decode('utf-8')
        gitignore_spec = pathspec.PathSpec.from_lines("gitwildmatch", gi_content.splitlines())

Step 4 — Recursive Content Fetching (1 API call per directory): 

def fetch_contents(path):
    url = f"https://api.github.com/repos/{owner}/{repo}/contents/{path}"
    params = {"ref": ref} if ref is not None else {}
    response = requests.get(url, headers=headers, params=params, timeout=(30, 30))

    # Rate limit handling with header-based wait:
    if response.status_code in (403, 429) and 'rate limit exceeded' in response.text.lower():
        if not token:
            raise Exception("GitHub API rate limit exceeded. Provide a token.")
        reset_time = int(response.headers.get('X-RateLimit-Reset', 0))
        wait_time = max(reset_time - time.time(), 0) + 1
        time.sleep(wait_time)
        return fetch_contents(path)  # Recursive retry

    contents = response.json()
    if not isinstance(contents, list):
        contents = [contents]

    for item in contents:
        if item["type"] == "file":
            # Check patterns, size, then fetch content
            # Path A: Use download_url directly, check Content-Length header
            # Path B (fallback): If no download_url, GET item["url"],
            #   base64 decode with size estimate: len(content) * 0.75 > max_file_size
        elif item["type"] == "dir":
            # Check gitignore + exclude before recursing
            fetch_contents(item["path"])

Step 5 — Dual Content Fetch Strategy: 

# Path A: download_url available
if "download_url" in item and item["download_url"]:
    file_response = requests.get(item["download_url"], headers=headers, timeout=(30, 30))
    content_length = int(file_response.headers.get('content-length', 0))
    if content_length > max_file_size:  # Final size check
        continue
    files[rel_path] = file_response.text

# Path B: base64 fallback
else:
    content_response = requests.get(item["url"], headers=headers, timeout=(30, 30))
    content_data = content_response.json()
    if len(content_data["content"]) * 0.75 > max_file_size:  # Approximate size
        continue
    file_content = base64.b64decode(content_data["content"]).decode('utf-8')
    files[rel_path] = file_content

Provide a GitHub token." | | 404 | Token, no path, ref='main' | "Repository not found. Check if default branch is not 'main'" | | 404 | Token, with path | "Path '{path}' not found or insufficient permissions." | | 403/429 | No token | Raise exception: "Rate limit exceeded. Provide a token." | | 403/429 | With token | Sleep using X-RateLimit-Reset header, recursive retry |

No LLM call. Routes to "direct" or "batch". Writes shared["max_tokens"], shared["file_batches"], shared["directory_tree"].

ContextRouter Algorithm: 1. Auto-detect max_tokens from provider if not set; write to shared["max_tokens"] 2. Measure prompt overhead = max(template_tokens for tutorial/advanced map_abstractions.md) + directory_tree_tokens 3. safety_limit = int(max_tokens * 0.95); effective_limit = safety_limit - prompt_overhead 4. Count total file content tokens using f"--- File Index {i}: {path} ---\n{content}\n\n" per file 5. If total_tokens > effective_limit OR force_batch: - Group files by os.path.dirname(path) — NEVER mix directories - Within each directory group, create batches respecting both effective_limit tokens AND batch_size file count - Return "batch" 6. Else: Return "direct"

dirname/
  filename.ext (idx:0)
  other.ext (idx:1)
other_dir/
  file.ext (idx:2)

\033[93m  [Debug] Batch {idx}: {len(batch)} files, ~{content_tokens:,} content tokens (limit: {effective_limit:,})\033[0m
\033[92m    - [{i}] {path}\033[0m

Notes for AI: Prompt templates are in prompts/tutorial/, prompts/advanced/, prompts/api-reference/, and prompts/sdk/. They contain {placeholder} variables that form a CONTRACT with the node code.

def load_prompt_template(template_name, advanced_mode=False, mode=None):
    """Load a prompt template file from the prompts/ directory."""
    if mode is None:

def create_token_counter():
    """Create a token counting function using tiktoken with char-count fallback."""
    try:
        enc = tiktoken.get_encoding("cl100k_base")
        return lambda text: len(enc.encode(text, disallowed_special=()))
    except Exception:
        return lambda text: len(text) // 4

docs.text:
Source File: flow.py

The flow.py module defines the core execution graph and workflow topology for the Codebase Knowledge Builder pipeline. It coordinates how repositories are ingested, how codebase contexts are routed across different processing strategies, and how educational chapter tutorials are synthesized, structured, and compiled into finalized Markdown documentation.

The module constructs a directed execution flow using the pocketflow orchestration framework, interconnecting modular processing units defined in nodes.

docs.title: Architectural Overview
docs.text:
The workflow returned by flow.py provides three distinct processing routes configured dynamically by repository characteristics and token budgets:

  1. Direct Path ("direct"): Used when the codebase fits within a standard prompt window, routing directly to abstraction identification.
  2. Batch Path ("batch"): Employs a Map-Reduce pipeline (MapAbstractions followed by ReduceAbstractions) to partition large codebases across multiple context windows before merging abstraction representations.
  3. Deterministic Path ("deterministic"): Bypasses dynamic abstraction clustering entirely, mapping individual source files directly into a 1:1 chapter layout (DeterministicFileMapper) before chapter generation.

All routes converge into chapter generation (WriteChapters) and final tutorial compilation (CombineTutorial).

Visibility: Public Signature: def create_tutorial_flow() -> Flow:

Description: Instantiates, configures, and links all processing nodes to produce the end-to-end tutorial generation pipeline. Node retry policies are configured with max_retries=5 and exponential backoff parameters (wait=20) to tolerate API rate limiting and transient upstream failures when calling LLM endpoints.

Parameters: None

Returns: * Flow: An initialized pocketflow.Flow pipeline instance with FetchRepo designated as the root entry point.

Raises: None directly raised during construction.* Execution-time exceptions are managed by individual node instances and pocketflow execution loops.

Example: 

def create_tutorial_flow():
    fetch_repo = FetchRepo()
    context_router = ContextRouter()
    map_abstractions = MapAbstractions(max_retries=5, wait=20)
    reduce_abstractions = ReduceAbstractions(max_retries=5, wait=20)
    identify_abstractions = IdentifyAbstractions(max_retries=5, wait=20)
    analyze_relationships = AnalyzeRelationships(max_retries=5, wait=20)
    order_chapters = OrderChapters(max_retries=5, wait=20)
    write_chapters = WriteChapters(max_retries=5, wait=20)
    combine_tutorial = CombineTutorial()
    deterministic_mapper = DeterministicFileMapper(max_retries=5, wait=20)

    fetch_repo >> context_router

    context_router - "direct" >> identify_abstractions
    context_router - "batch" >> map_abstractions
    context_router - "deterministic" >> deterministic_mapper

    map_abstractions >> reduce_abstractions

    identify_abstractions >> analyze_relationships
    reduce_abstractions >> analyze_relationships

    analyze_relationships >> order_chapters
    order_chapters >> write_chapters

    deterministic_mapper >> write_chapters

    write_chapters >> combine_tutorial

    return Flow(start=fetch_repo)

The function instantiates eight specialized LLM-backed node instances with retry and backoff properties, along with two local control-flow nodes (FetchRepo and CombineTutorial). It establishes conditional transitions using pocketflow syntax (>> for sequential binding, - "action" >> for conditional branch targets). The resulting graph ensures that regardless of repository scale, the shared downstream synthesis nodes (WriteChapters and CombineTutorial) receive a consistent shared context payload.

docs.title: Stage 1: Ingestion and Branch Selection
docs.text:
1. FetchRepo: Ingests files from either local filesystem paths or remote GitHub repositories using utilities defined in utils.crawl_local_files and utils.crawl_github_files.
  2. ContextRouter: Inspects the total token volume and structure of the ingested repository, returning one of three action strings:
  3. "direct": Dispatched when the entire codebase fits comfortably within single-pass LLM context windows.
  4. "batch": Dispatched when token volume necessitates partitioning across chunked map-reduce passes.
  5. "deterministic": Dispatched when file-by-file chapter parity is requested.

docs.title: Stage 2: Abstraction Mapping and Relationships
docs.text: Depending on the routing action selected in Stage 1: - Direct Route: IdentifyAbstractions extracts architectural abstractions in a single pass. - Batch Route: MapAbstractions scans repository slices in parallel or sequential batches, which ReduceAbstractions then consolidates into a single unified conceptual index. - Both routes feed into AnalyzeRelationships to discover dependency relationships, followed by OrderChapters to determine optimal pedagogical sequence. - Deterministic Route: DeterministicFileMapper maps source files directly to individual chapter outlines without intermediate semantic clustering.

docs.title: Stage 3: Chapter Synthesis and Compilation
docs.text:
1. WriteChapters: Consumes the chapter outlines (from either OrderChapters or DeterministicFileMapper) and concurrently prompts the model to generate detailed Markdown chapters incorporating code snippets, diagrams, and deep technical prose.
  2. CombineTutorial: Aggregates all completed chapter outputs, builds a table of contents, resolves cross-chapter index links, and writes the complete document structure to disk.

docs.title: Technical Overview
docs.text:
main.py is the primary entry point and command-line interface (CLI) for the Codebase-Knowledge-Builder application. It coordinates the end-to-end execution lifecycle for converting codebases (either remote GitHub repositories or local directories) into structured architectural tutorials, advanced developer guides, API references, or SDK documentation suites.

The script performs the following core responsibilities: 1. Environment Initialization: Loads environment variables from .env files via dotenv.load_dotenv() to configure LLM API keys and service endpoints. 2. CLI Parameter Parsing & Validation: Configures and evaluates command-line arguments using argparse, enforcing mutual exclusivity between repository URLs (--repo) and local directories (--dir), while applying validation rules (such as restricting --incremental caching strictly to --mode api-reference). 3. Exclusion & Inclusion Pattern Aggregation: Merges custom user pattern filters with comprehensive built-in defaults that encompass binaries, dependencies, build caches, test suites, IDE artifacts, and AI agent configuration files. 4. Shared State Construction: Builds the central mutable shared state dictionary containing runtime settings, file filters, documentation modes, and output buffers passed across all workflow nodes. 5. LLM & Logging Diagnostics: Queries model endpoint metadata and context window limits via get_model_context_length, configures per-run logging via configure_logging, and outputs execution summaries to stdout. 6. Pipeline Dispatch & Post-Processing: Invokes create_tutorial_flow() from flow, executes the sequential processing graph with tutorial_flow.run(shared), and handles optional post-run cache or log teardown if --cleanup is specified.

docs.title: DEFAULT_INCLUDE_PATTERNS
docs.text:
• Type: set[str]
  • Value: {"*"}
  • Description: The default glob pattern set used when the user does not specify explicit inclusion rules via -i or --include. It matches all discovered files in the target directory tree.

docs.title: DEFAULT_EXCLUDE_PATTERNS
docs.text:
• Type: set[str]
  • Description: A comprehensive set of glob patterns automatically ignored during repository traversal. When custom exclude patterns are provided via -e or --exclude, they are combined with this set via set union. It prevents non-source assets, build artifacts, environments, and tool caches from polluting LLM context windows.

The patterns are grouped internally into 7 distinct categories: 1. Media, Data, and Static Assets: Binary media files, document formats, archives, and web assets (e.g., assets/*, data/*, *.png, *.mp4, *.pdf, *.zip, *.tar). 2. Build, Distribution, and Framework Caches: Compiler and framework output directories (e.g., dist/*, build/*, target/*, .next/*, .nuxt/*, *.log, *.tmp). 3. Environments, Dependencies & Lockfiles: Package managers, virtual environments, and lockfiles (e.g., venv/*, .venv/*, node_modules/*, vendor/*, package-lock.json, Cargo.lock, poetry.lock). 4. Language-Specific Exclusions: Bytecode, compiled binaries, and test coverage outputs across Python, Java/JVM, and C/C++ (e.g., __pycache__/*, *.pyc, *.class, *.jar, *.o, *.so, *.dylib, ios/Pods/*, android/.gradle/*). 5. OS & Version Control: System metadata and VCS internals (e.g., .git/*, .github/*, .DS_Store, Thumbs.db). 6. Classic IDEs: Workspace settings for development environments (e.g., .vscode/*, .idea/*, *.iml, .vs/*). 7. AI Agents & Modern AI IDEs: Context files, rulesets, and scratchpads generated by coding assistants (e.g., .cursor/*, .cursorrules, .windsurf/*, .cline/*, .roo/*, .agent/*, .continue/*, .claude/*, .copilot/*).

docs.text:
Visibility: Public Signature: def main() -> None:

Description: Serves as the master CLI execution function. It configures the argparse.ArgumentParser instance with all operational flags, validates arguments, resolves project metadata, constructs the shared state dictionary, configures diagnostic logging, executes the pipeline flow graph, and executes optional teardown operations.

Parameters: * None (reads from sys.argv and system environment variables).

Returns: * None

Raises: * SystemExit: Raised by argparse upon missing required arguments (--repo or --dir), invalid command syntax, or when invoked with --help. * Exception: Any uncaught exceptions propagated during node execution inside tutorial_flow.run(shared).

docs.title: 1. CLI Parsing & Mutually Exclusive Source Selection
docs.text:
def main():
    parser = argparse.ArgumentParser(description="Generate a tutorial for a GitHub codebase or local directory.")

    # Create mutually exclusive group for source
    source_group = parser.add_mutually_exclusive_group(required=True)
    source_group.add_argument("--repo", help="URL of the public GitHub repository.")
    source_group.add_argument("--dir", help="Path to local directory.")

    parser.add_argument("-n", "--name", help="Project name (optional, derived from repo/directory if omitted).")
    parser.add_argument("-t", "--token", help="GitHub personal access token (optional, reads from GITHUB_TOKEN env var if not provided).")
    parser.add_argument("-o", "--output", default="output", help="Base directory for output (default: ./output).")
    parser.add_argument("-i", "--include", nargs="+", help="Files to include (e.g., '*.py' '*.js'). Defaults to '*' (all files).")
    parser.add_argument(
        "-e",
        "--exclude",
        nargs="+",
        help="Files to exclude. Custom patterns are automatically merged with a massive global exclusion list (build caches, node_modules, binaries, media, AI environments) AND your repository's native .gitignore rules.",
    )
    parser.add_argument("-s", "--max-size", type=int, default=200000, help="Maximum file size in bytes (default: 200000, about 200KB).")
    # ...

The CLI entry initializes an argparse.ArgumentParser configured with a required mutually exclusive group for input target resolution: either --repo (for remote GitHub repositories) or --dir (for local file system paths). File traversal options allow setting base directories, file size ceilings in bytes (defaulting to 200,000 bytes / ~200 KB), and glob-based inclusion/exclusion lists.

Flags like --mkdocs alter document output structures for static documentation site generators. Granular parameters govern batch size for map-reduce flows, context token limits, LLM reasoning effort levels, cache invalidation, and incremental rebuild toggling.

docs.title: 3. Validation, Auth Discovery, and Cache Manifest Management
docs.text:
# ...
    # Get GitHub token from argument or environment variable if using repo
    github_token = None
    if args.repo:
        github_token = args.token or os.environ.get("GITHUB_TOKEN")
        if not github_token:
            print("Warning: No GitHub token provided. You might hit rate limits for public repositories.")

    # Resolve mode (backward compatibility for --advanced)
    doc_mode = "advanced" if args.advanced else args.mode

    # Enforce incremental cache constraints
    if args.incremental and doc_mode != "api-reference":
        print(
            "\n\033[93m[Warning] --incremental caching is only effective in 'api-reference' mode due to stable 1:1 file mapping. Disabling incremental cache for this run.\033[0m\n"
        )
        args.incremental = False

    # Handle --force-rebuild: delete the cache manifest to force fresh generation
    if args.force_rebuild and args.incremental:
        project_name = args.name
        if not project_name:
            # Derive project name the same way FetchRepo does
            if args.dir:
                project_name = os.path.basename(os.path.abspath(args.dir))
            elif args.repo:
                project_name = args.repo.rstrip("/").split("/")[-1]
        if project_name:
            output_base = args.output or "output"
            manifest_path = os.path.join(output_base, project_name, ".doc_cache_manifest.json")
            if os.path.exists(manifest_path):
                os.remove(manifest_path)
                print(f"\033[93m[Force Rebuild] Deleted cache manifest: {manifest_path}\033[0m")
            else:
                print(f"\033[93m[Force Rebuild] No cache manifest found at {manifest_path} — all chapters will be generated fresh.\033[0m")
    elif args.force_rebuild and not args.incremental:
        print("\033[93m[Warning] --force-rebuild has no effect without --incremental. Ignoring.\033[0m")
    # ...

Post-parsing validation extracts GitHub personal access tokens from --token or the GITHUB_TOKEN environment variable. Mode resolution reconciles legacy --advanced flags. Incremental caching (--incremental) is strictly validated: because only api-reference mode guarantees stable 1:1 module-to-chapter file mapping, incremental generation is disabled with a warning in other modes. If --force-rebuild is supplied alongside --incremental, the runtime derives the output path and removes .doc_cache_manifest.json to invalidate cached module hashes.

docs.title: get_content_for_indices()
docs.text:
Visibility: Public Signature: def get_content_for_indices(files_data: list[tuple[str, str]], indices: list[int]) -> dict[str, str]:

Description: Resolves file index numbers into a formatted mapping of file identifiers and their associated raw source contents. It creates a dictionary where keys use the composite index format {index} # {path}, ensuring downstream prompt generators receive clear positional anchors.

Parameters: * files_data (list[tuple[str, str]]): Sequence of (path, content) tuples representing all crawled project source files. * indices (list[int]): List of integer indices corresponding to the target files needed for context.

Returns: * dict[str, str]: Mapping of structured index keys ("{i} # {path}") to raw file contents.

Example: 

def get_content_for_indices(files_data, indices):
    content_map = {}
    for i in indices:
        if 0 <= i < len(files_data):
            path, content = files_data[i]
            content_map[f"{i} # {path}"] = content  # Use index + path as key for context
    return content_map

The function checks index bounds (0 <= i < len(files_data)) to prevent IndexError exceptions during lookups if an LLM outputs out-of-range indices. Any index outside the valid range is ignored silently.

Visibility: Public Signature: def load_prompt_template(template_name: str, advanced_mode: bool = False, mode: str = None) -> str:

Description: Reads Markdown prompt template files stored on disk in the prompts/ subdirectories. It resolves directory hierarchy based on the requested execution mode (tutorial, advanced, or custom mode strings) and ensures correct character encoding during read operations.

Parameters: * template_name (str): Base filename of the target prompt template (without the .md extension). * advanced_mode (bool): Fallback flag used if mode is None to toggle between advanced and tutorial directories. * mode (str): Target subfolder name inside prompts/ (e.g., "tutorial", "advanced", "api-reference", "sdk").

Returns: * str: Raw template content string loaded from disk.

docs.text:
Visibility: Public Signature: def parse_yaml_response(response: str) -> object:

Description: Extracts fenced YAML blocks (```yaml ... ```) from model responses and parses them into native Python data structures using PyYAML's safe_load.

Parameters: * response (str): Raw text response generated by the LLM.

Returns: * object: Parsed YAML structure (list, dict, or scalar values).

Raises: * ValueError: When the response string does not contain valid `yaml ` markers or contains unparseable YAML syntax.

Example: 

def parse_yaml_response(response):
    """Extract and parse YAML from an LLM response fenced in ```yaml blocks."""
    try:
        yaml_str = response.strip().split("```yaml")[1].split("```")[0].strip()
        return yaml.safe_load(yaml_str)
    except Exception as e:
        raise ValueError(f"Failed to parse YAML: {e}") from e

This extraction strategy splits the string strictly by the yaml``` block delimiter and extracts everything before the closing `` delimiter. If a model fails to wrap its output within explicit YAML fences, index operations raise an IndexError, which is caught and re-raised as a ValueError to trigger pocketflow retry loops.

docs.text:
Visibility: Public Signature: def create_token_counter() -> collections.abc.Callable[[str], int]:

Description: Instantiates a fast token counting callable using the tiktoken library parameterized with the cl100k_base BPE tokenizer encoding. It provides an inline fallback heuristic (len(text) // 4) if tiktoken encounters an import or initialization failure.

Returns: * Callable[[str], int]: A function accepting a string and returning its calculated token length.

Example: 

def create_token_counter():
    """Create a token counting function using tiktoken with char-count fallback."""
    try:
        enc = tiktoken.get_encoding("cl100k_base")
        return lambda text: len(enc.encode(text, disallowed_special=()))
    except Exception:
        return lambda text: len(text) // 4

The closure disables special token validation via disallowed_special=() to ensure arbitrary source code containing patterns like <|endoftext|> can be tokenized safely without raising exceptions.

def resolve_max_tokens(shared):

    max_tokens = shared.get("max_tokens")
    if max_tokens is not None:
        return max_tokens
    provider = os.environ.get("LLM_PROVIDER")
    if provider == "GEMINI" or not provider:

        model_name = os.environ.get(f"{provider}_MODEL", "")
        api_key = os.environ.get(f"{provider}_API_KEY", "")

docs.text:
Visibility: Public Signature: def prep(self, shared: dict) -> tuple:

Description: Calculates token consumption across templates, directory trees, and source files. It checks context limits against resolve_max_tokens(shared) using a 95% safety margin.

Parameters: * shared (dict): Pipeline shared store.

Returns: * tuple: Structured routing tuple specifying the target branch and budget constraints.

Example: 

    def prep(self, shared):
        files_data = shared["files"]
        max_tokens = resolve_max_tokens(shared)

        shared["max_tokens"] = max_tokens

        # --- Token estimation setup ---
        count_tokens = create_token_counter()

        # --- Calculate prompt overhead FIRST ---
        # 1. Prompt template (measure both, use the larger)
        prompt_dir = os.path.join(os.path.dirname(os.path.abspath(__file__)), "prompts")
        max_template_tokens = 0
        for subdir in ["tutorial", "advanced"]:
            template_path = os.path.join(prompt_dir, subdir, "map_abstractions.md")
            if os.path.exists(template_path):
                with open(template_path, encoding="utf-8-sig") as f:
                    t = count_tokens(f.read())
                max_template_tokens = max(max_template_tokens, t)

        # 2. Directory tree (built from all files, shared across batches)
        directory_tree = self._build_directory_tree(files_data)
        tree_tokens = count_tokens(directory_tree)

        # 3. File listing index (e.g. "- 0 # main.py\n- 1 # nodes.py\n...")
        file_listing_str = "\n".join(f"- {i} # {path}" for i, (path, _) in enumerate(files_data))
        listing_tokens = count_tokens(file_listing_str)

        prompt_overhead = max_template_tokens + tree_tokens + listing_tokens
        // ...
        # --- Effective limit = safety margin minus overhead ---
        safety_limit = int(max_tokens * 0.95)
        effective_limit = safety_limit - prompt_overhead
        force_batch = shared.get("force_batch", False)

        if shared.get("mode", "tutorial") == "api-reference":
            return ("deterministic", files_data, effective_limit, shared.get("batch_size", 50), None, None, directory_tree, False)

        if total_tokens <= effective_limit and not force_batch:
            return ("direct", files_data, effective_limit, shared.get("batch_size", 50), None, None, directory_tree, False)

        return (
            "batch",
            files_data,
            effective_limit,
            shared.get("batch_size", 50),
            file_token_map,
            count_tokens,
            directory_tree,
            shared.get("debug", False),
        )

The node calculates prompt overhead before checking content tokens to protect against context truncation. It computes the maximum overhead between tutorial and advanced prompts and measures tree and listing sizes to determine the effective_limit.

docs.title: ContextRouter.exec()
docs.text:
Visibility: Public Signature: def exec(self, prep_res: tuple) -> str | list[list[tuple[int, str, str]]]:

Description: Executes routing logic. In "batch" mode, it groups files by directory and splits them into token-budgeted batches without mixing directories.

Parameters: * prep_res (tuple): Parameter tuple returned by ContextRouter.prep().

Returns: * str | list[list[tuple[int, str, str]]]: Returns routing keys ("direct", "deterministic") or a nested list of file batches.

Example: 

    def exec(self, prep_res):
        route, files_data, effective_limit, batch_size, file_token_map, _count_tokens, directory_tree, debug = prep_res
        llm_logger.info(
            f"NODE EXEC | node=ContextRouter | action=route_decision | route={route} | files={len(files_data)} | effective_limit={effective_limit:,}"
        )

        if route == "direct":
            return "direct"
        if route == "deterministic":
            return "deterministic"

        # Group by directory for coherence, with pre-computed tokens
        dir_groups = defaultdict(list)
        for i, (path, content) in enumerate(files_data):
            dir_groups[os.path.dirname(path)].append((i, path, content, file_token_map[i]))

        # Build token-aware batches (never mix directories)
        batches = []
        for dirname in sorted(dir_groups.keys()):
            current_batch = []
            current_tokens = 0

            for i, path, content, tokens in dir_groups[dirname]:
                # Start new batch if adding this file would exceed effective limit or file count cap
                if current_batch and (current_tokens + tokens > effective_limit or len(current_batch) >= batch_size):
                    batches.append(current_batch)
                    current_batch = []
                    current_tokens = 0

                current_batch.append((i, path, content))
                current_tokens += tokens

            # Flush remaining files in this directory
            if current_batch:
                batches.append(current_batch)

        self._directory_tree = directory_tree
        return batches

The batching algorithm preserves directory boundaries to maintain architectural locality. Files in the same folder are grouped together until they hit effective_limit or batch_size.

Visibility: Private / Protected Static Signature: def _build_directory_tree(files_data: list[tuple[str, str]]) -> str:

Returns: * str: Formatted directory hierarchy representation.

Example: 

    @staticmethod
    def _build_directory_tree(files_data):
        """Build a compact directory tree string from the list of (path, content) tuples."""
        from collections import defaultdict

        dir_files = defaultdict(list)
        for i, (path, _content) in enumerate(files_data):
            dirname = os.path.dirname(path) or "."
            basename = os.path.basename(path)
            dir_files[dirname].append(f"{basename} (idx:{i})")

            lines.extend(f"  {fname}" for fname in sorted(dir_files[dirname]))

Visibility: Public Signature: def prep(self, shared: dict) -> tuple:

Description: Computes token-aware code snippet inclusions for each abstraction using two-pass budget balancing, preventing later abstractions from being starved of context.

Parameters: * shared (dict): Pipeline shared store.

Returns: * tuple: Formatted context payload and abstraction listings.

Example: 

    def prep(self, shared):
        abstractions = shared["abstractions"]
        files_data = shared["files"]
        project_name = shared["project_name"]
        language = shared.get("language", "english")
        use_cache = shared.get("use_cache", True)
        thinking_level = shared.get("thinking_level", None)

        max_tokens = shared.get("max_tokens", 100000)
        safety_limit = int(max_tokens * 0.95)
        prompt_overhead = 2000

        estimate_tokens = create_token_counter()
        // ...
        per_abstr_budget = total_budget // max(num_abstractions, 1)
        included_indices = set()
        abstr_results = []

        # Pass 1: give each abstraction an equal share, track unused
        for _i, sized in enumerate(abstr_file_data):
            budget = per_abstr_budget
            included_files = []
            remaining_files = []
            for idx, path, file_content, tokens in sized:
                if idx in included_indices:
                    included_files.append((idx, path, None, 0))
                    continue
                if tokens <= budget:
                    included_files.append((idx, path, file_content, tokens))
                    budget -= tokens
                    included_indices.add(idx)
                else:
                    remaining_files.append((idx, path, file_content, tokens))
            abstr_results.append((included_files, remaining_files, budget))

        # Pass 2: redistribute unused budget to abstractions that need more
        total_unused = sum(r[2] for r in abstr_results)
        if total_unused > 0:
            for i, (included_files, remaining_files, _unused) in enumerate(abstr_results):
                if not remaining_files or total_unused <= 0:
                    continue
                still_remaining = []
                for idx, path, file_content, tokens in remaining_files:
                    if idx in included_indices:
                        included_files.append((idx, path, None, 0))
                        continue
                    if tokens <= total_unused:
                        included_files.append((idx, path, file_content, tokens))
                        total_unused -= tokens
                        included_indices.add(idx)
                    else:
                        still_remaining.append((idx, path, file_content, tokens))
                abstr_results[i] = (included_files, still_remaining, 0)
        // ...
        return (
            context,
            "\n".join(abstraction_info_for_prompt),
            num_abstractions,
            project_name,
            language,
            use_cache,
            thinking_level,
            shared.get("advanced_mode", False),
            shared.get("max_tokens", 100000),
            shared.get("mode", "tutorial"),
        )

The two-pass allocator sorts files in each abstraction by size (largest first) and distributes context evenly. In the second pass, leftover tokens from smaller modules roll over to larger abstractions that need more budget.

Parameters: * prep_res (tuple): Parameter bundle from prep().

Example: 

    def exec(self, prep_res):

            (
                abstraction_listing,
                context,

            prompt = prompt_template.format(
                project_name=project_name, list_lang_note=list_lang_note, abstraction_listing=abstraction_listing, context=context
            )
            log_token_estimation(self.__class__.__name__, prompt, max_tokens)
            response = call_llm(prompt, use_cache=(use_cache and self.cur_retry == 0), thinking_level=thinking_level)

            ordered_indices_raw = parse_yaml_response(response)
            if not isinstance(ordered_indices_raw, list):
                raise ValueError("LLM output is not a list")

            ordered_indices = []
            seen_indices = set()
            for entry in ordered_indices_raw:
                idx = int(str(entry).split("#")[0].strip())
                if not (0 <= idx < num_abstractions):
                    raise ValueError(f"Invalid index {idx} in ordered list. Max index is {num_abstractions - 1}.")
                if idx in seen_indices:
                    raise ValueError(f"Duplicate index {idx} found in ordered list.")
                ordered_indices.append(idx)
                seen_indices.add(idx)

            if len(ordered_indices) != num_abstractions:
                raise ValueError(f"Ordered list length mismatch. Missing: {set(range(num_abstractions)) - seen_indices}")

            return ordered_indices
        except Exception as e:

    def prep(self, shared):

            if 0 <= abstraction_index < len(abstractions):
                chapter_num = i + 1
                chapter_name = abstractions[abstraction_index]["name"].replace("\n", " ").strip()
                is_mkdocs = shared.get("mkdocs", False)

                    filename = doc_rel_path.replace(os.sep, "/")
                elif is_mkdocs:
                    safe_name = "".join(c if c.isalnum() else "_" for c in chapter_name).lower()
                    filename = f"{safe_name}.md"
                else:
                    safe_name = "".join(c if c.isalnum() else "_" for c in chapter_name).lower()

                next_chapter = chapter_filenames[chapter_order[i + 1]] if i < len(chapter_order) - 1 else None

    def exec(self, item):

            chapter_num = item["chapter_num"]
            project_name = item.get("project_name")

            file_context_str = "\n\n".join(
                f"--- File: {idx_path.split('# ')[1] if '# ' in idx_path else idx_path} ---\n{content}"
                for idx_path, content in item["related_files_content_map"].items()
            )

            # --- Incremental Caching Logic ---
            current_hash = None
            if incremental and output_dir:
                import hashlib, json
                hasher = hashlib.md5()
                hasher.update(file_context_str.encode("utf-8"))
                current_hash = hasher.hexdigest()

                manifest_path = os.path.join(output_dir, project_name, ".doc_cache_manifest.json")
                if os.path.exists(manifest_path):
                    try:
                        with open(manifest_path, encoding="utf-8") as f:
                            manifest = json.load(f)
                        if manifest.get(abstraction_name) == current_hash:
                            file_path = os.path.join(output_dir, project_name, "docs", "api", filename) if is_mkdocs else os.path.join(output_dir, project_name, filename)
                            if os.path.exists(file_path):

                                    cached_content = f.read()
                                clean_content = cached_content
                                if is_mkdocs and clean_content.startswith("---"):
                                    parts = clean_content.split("---", 2)
                                    if len(parts) >= 3:
                                        clean_content = parts[2].strip()
                                self.chapters_written_so_far.append(clean_content)
                                return {"content": clean_content, "hash": current_hash, "name": abstraction_name}
                    except Exception as e:
                        print(f"Warning: Failed to read manifest cache: {e}")

            previous_chapters_summary = "" if doc_mode == "api-reference" else "\n---\n".join(self.chapter_summaries)
            prompt_template = load_prompt_template("draft_chapters", mode=doc_mode)
            prompt = prompt_template.format(
                language_instruction="",
                project_name=project_name,
                abstraction_name=abstraction_name,
                chapter_num=chapter_num,

                link_lang_note="",
                code_comment_note="",
                mermaid_lang_note="",
                tone_note="",
            )

            chapter_content = call_llm(prompt, use_cache=(use_cache and self.cur_retry == 0), thinking_level=thinking_level)
            self.chapters_written_so_far.append(chapter_content)

            if doc_mode != "api-reference":
                summary_prompt = build_chapter_summary_prompt(chapter_num, abstraction_name, chapter_content, language)
                chapter_summary = call_llm(summary_prompt, use_cache=True, thinking_level=None)
                self.chapter_summaries.append(f"Chapter {chapter_num} — {abstraction_name.strip()}:\n{chapter_summary}")

                        f.write(chapter_info["content"])

                # Create full_content.md

docs.title: Technical Overview
docs.text:
The utils/__init__.py file serves as the package initialization marker for the utils namespace within the Codebase-Knowledge-Builder repository. In Python's module architecture, an __init__.py file designates its enclosing directory as an importable regular package, establishing the namespace hierarchy that permits explicit sub-module resolution (e.g., from utils.call_llm import call_llm).

In Codebase-Knowledge-Builder, utils/__init__.py is maintained as a clean, zero-byte module initialization file. It does not perform eager re-exports, runtime symbol definitions, or package-level state initialization. This design pattern ensures: 1. Decoupled Imports and Zero Side Effects: Importing individual utility sub-modules does not trigger unintended side effects or instantiate unneeded dependencies across unrelated execution paths. 2. Elimination of Circular Dependencies: Downstream processing nodes and orchestration layers can selectively consume specific utility functions without inducing circular reference chains between utility submodules and pipeline components. 3. Lazy Submodule Loading: Modules such as utils.call_llm, utils.crawl_github_files, utils.crawl_local_files, utils.prompts, and utils.token_utils are loaded into sys.modules strictly on demand.

docs.title: Key Architectural Capabilities
docs.text:
1. Dual Provider Routing:
  2. Google Gemini Engine: Direct integration via the modern google-genai SDK (google.genai), supporting both API key authentication and Google Cloud Vertex AI infrastructure (GEMINI_PROJECT_ID, GEMINI_LOCATION).
  3. OpenAI-Compatible Endpoint Engine: Generic HTTP client capable of communicating with standard /v1/chat/completions REST endpoints, including local Ollama runtimes and OpenRouter proxy networks.
  4. Response Caching: Deterministic local caching using an llm_cache.json flat-file registry to eliminate redundant token consumption and expedite debugging across repetitive workflow executions.
  5. Reasoning and Extended Thinking Support: Translates abstract reasoning requests (thinking_level in low, medium, high) to underlying engine configurations:
  6. For Gemini: Sets types.ThinkingConfig(thinking_budget=...).
  7. For OpenRouter: Validates provider capabilities dynamically against the OpenRouter API and attaches reasoning: {"effort": ...} payloads.
  8. For Ollama: Injects both think and reasoning_effort parameters.
  9. Context Length Discovery: Programmatically fetches model context limits via get_model_context_length to facilitate safe token chunking and batch management upstream in token_utils.
  10. Run-Isolated Logging: Implements a two-phase logging lifecycle using Python's standard logging library. Logging is absorbed via logging.NullHandler at import time and activated per-run into timestamped files via configure_logging.

docs.title: configure_logging()
docs.text:
Visibility: Public Signature: def configure_logging(project_name="project", mode="tutorial") -> str:

Description: Configures file-based logging for the active execution run. It creates a dedicated directory (defaulting to logs/ or sourced from the LOG_DIR environment variable) and initializes a logging.FileHandler using a timestamped filename format: {safe_project}_{safe_mode}_{YYYYMMDD_HHmmss}.log. Any existing handlers on logger (such as the default import-time NullHandler) are cleared prior to attaching the file handler. It writes run initialization banners containing execution metadata directly to the log file.

Parameters: * project_name (str, optional): Identifier for the target project being analyzed. Sanitized to alphanumeric, dash, dot, and underscore characters. Defaults to "project". * mode (str, optional): Execution mode or workflow profile. Hyphens are replaced with underscores. Defaults to "tutorial".

Returns: * str: The absolute or relative filesystem path of the initialized log file.

Raises: * OSError: If the directory specified in LOG_DIR cannot be created.

Implementation: 

def configure_logging(project_name="project", mode="tutorial"):
    log_directory = os.getenv("LOG_DIR", "logs")
    os.makedirs(log_directory, exist_ok=True)

    # Sanitize project name for filesystem safety
    safe_project = "".join(c if c.isalnum() or c in "-_." else "_" for c in project_name)
    safe_mode = mode.replace("-", "_")
    timestamp = datetime.now().strftime("%Y%m%d_%H%M%S")
    log_file = os.path.join(log_directory, f"{safe_project}_{safe_mode}_{timestamp}.log")

    # Remove any existing handlers (e.g., NullHandler) and add the file handler
    logger.handlers.clear()
    file_handler = logging.FileHandler(log_file, encoding="utf-8")
    file_handler.setFormatter(logging.Formatter("%(asctime)s - %(levelname)s - %(message)s"))
    logger.addHandler(file_handler)

    # Log run metadata at the start of every log file
    logger.info(f"{'=' * 80}")
    logger.info(f"RUN STARTED | project={project_name} | mode={mode} | timestamp={timestamp}")
    logger.info(f"Log file: {log_file}")
    logger.info(f"{'=' * 80}")

    return log_file

The function provides predictable log isolation across multiple parallel or sequential pipeline invocations. It sanitizes user-supplied project names by filtering non-standard filesystem characters to prevent directory traversal or malformed file paths. The log format includes full millisecond timestamps, logging severity levels, and structured informational banners.

docs.text:
Visibility: Private Signature: def _get_openrouter_model_info(model_id: str) -> dict | None:

Description: Retrieves model capability metadata from OpenRouter's public model catalog endpoint (https://openrouter.ai/api/v1/models). Results are cached within the module-level _openrouter_models_cache variable to avoid redundant network round-trips across consecutive model invocations.

Parameters: * model_id (str): The unique identifier of the target model (e.g., "anthropic/claude-3.7-sonnet").

Returns: * dict | None: The dictionary containing model metadata (such as reasoning support, pricing, and context limits), or None if the model cannot be found or the network request fails.

Raises: * No exceptions are raised; network and parsing errors default _openrouter_models_cache to an empty list.

Implementation: 

def _get_openrouter_model_info(model_id: str) -> dict:
    global _openrouter_models_cache
    if _openrouter_models_cache is None:
        try:
            resp = requests.get("https://openrouter.ai/api/v1/models", timeout=5)
            _openrouter_models_cache = resp.json().get("data", [])
        except Exception:
            _openrouter_models_cache = []

    return next((m for m in _openrouter_models_cache if m.get("id") == model_id), None)

The function protects network latency during high-volume generation loops by using a lazy global cache pattern. It applies a 5-second connection and read timeout to ensure transient connectivity issues do not stall execution indefinitely.

docs.title: get_model_context_length()
docs.text:
Visibility: Public Signature: def get_model_context_length(endpoint_url: str, model_name: str, api_key: str = "") -> int:

Description: Determines the maximum token context window supported by a given model and endpoint. For Google Gemini endpoints or model names containing "gemini", it defaults to 1,000,000 tokens. For OpenRouter endpoints, it queries https://openrouter.ai/api/v1/models to extract the exact context_length property. For other configurations or on failure, it falls back to a safe default of 100,000 tokens.

Parameters: * endpoint_url (str): The base or endpoint URL configured for inference requests. * model_name (str): The name or identifier of the LLM model. * api_key (str, optional): Authorization token (reserved for future authenticated catalog endpoints). Defaults to "".

Returns: * int: The maximum token context length supported by the model.

Raises: * No exceptions are raised; unexpected failures emit warnings to logger and return 100000.

Implementation: 

def get_model_context_length(endpoint_url: str, model_name: str, api_key: str = "") -> int:
    default_limit = 100000
    try:
        if not endpoint_url:
            return default_limit

        if "generativelanguage.googleapis.com" in endpoint_url or "gemini" in model_name.lower():
            # Safely default to 1M tokens for Gemini models
            return 1000000

        if "openrouter.ai" in endpoint_url:
            resp = requests.get("https://openrouter.ai/api/v1/models", timeout=5)
            data = resp.json().get("data", [])
            for m in data:
                if m.get("id") == model_name:
                    return m.get("context_length", default_limit)
    except Exception as e:
        logger.warning(f"Failed to fetch context length for {model_name} at {endpoint_url}: {e}")

    return default_limit

This method is utilized by upstream partitioning algorithms to prevent token overflow exceptions during ingestion. By distinguishing Gemini's large-scale window from standard OpenAI/Ollama limits, callers can accurately maximize payload sizes.

docs.title: _call_llm_provider()
docs.text:
Visibility: Private Signature: def _call_llm_provider(prompt: str, thinking_level: str | None = None) -> str:

Description: Executes a chat completion request against an OpenAI-compatible HTTP REST endpoint (e.g., OpenRouter, Ollama, LocalAI). It reads runtime configurations from environment variables dynamically based on LLM_PROVIDER: * {provider}_MODEL: Model name. * {provider}_BASE_URL: Base host URL (e.g., http://localhost:11434). * {provider}_API_KEY: API key for authorization headers.

It normalizes URLs to append /v1/chat/completions, constructs authorization and JSON payload headers, applies vendor-specific reasoning effort parameters, and executes a requests.post call with a dual timeout (10, 300) (10s connection, 300s read).

Parameters: * prompt (str): The raw text prompt sent as a user message. * thinking_level (str | None, optional): Desired reasoning effort level (e.g., "low", "medium", "high"). Defaults to None.

Returns: * str: The textual content response extracted from choices[0].message.content.

Raises: * ValueError: If LLM_PROVIDER, {provider}_MODEL, or {provider}_BASE_URL are unset; if the server response is invalid JSON; or if the response lacks expected choices fields. * Exception: Standardized wrapping for requests.exceptions.HTTPError, requests.exceptions.ConnectionError, requests.exceptions.Timeout, and requests.exceptions.RequestException.

Implementation: 

def _call_llm_provider(prompt: str, thinking_level: str | None = None) -> str:
    # Read the provider from environment variable
    provider = os.environ.get("LLM_PROVIDER")
    if not provider:
        raise ValueError("LLM_PROVIDER environment variable is required")

    model_var = f"{provider}_MODEL"
    base_url_var = f"{provider}_BASE_URL"
    api_key_var = f"{provider}_API_KEY"

    model = os.environ.get(model_var)
    base_url = os.environ.get(base_url_var)
    api_key = os.environ.get(api_key_var, "")

    if not model:
        raise ValueError(f"{model_var} environment variable is required")
    if not base_url:
        raise ValueError(f"{base_url_var} environment variable is required")

    url = f"{base_url.rstrip('/')}/v1/chat/completions"
    headers = {"Content-Type": "application/json"}
    if api_key:
        headers["Authorization"] = f"Bearer {api_key}"

    payload = {
        "model": model,
        "messages": [{"role": "user", "content": prompt}],
        "temperature": 0.7,
    }

    if provider == "OPENROUTER" and thinking_level:
        model_info = _get_openrouter_model_info(model)
        if model_info and "reasoning" in model_info:
            supported_efforts = model_info["reasoning"].get("supported_efforts", [])
            if thinking_level.lower() in supported_efforts:
                payload["reasoning"] = {"effort": thinking_level.lower()}
                payload["temperature"] = 1.0
            else:
                logger.warning(f"Invalid thinking level '{thinking_level}' for model {model}. Supported efforts: {supported_efforts}")
        else:
            logger.warning(f"Model {model} does not support reasoning via OpenRouter API.")

    elif provider == "OLLAMA" and thinking_level:
        payload["think"] = thinking_level.lower()
        payload["reasoning_effort"] = thinking_level.lower()
        payload["temperature"] = 1.0

    try:
        response = requests.post(url, headers=headers, json=payload, timeout=(10, 300))
        try:
            response_json = response.json()
        except (ValueError, requests.exceptions.JSONDecodeError):
            print(f"\033[93mWarning: Provider returned invalid JSON. Status Code: {response.status_code}, Response Text: {response.text}\033[0m")
            logger.warning(f"Provider returned invalid JSON. Status Code: {response.status_code}, Response Text: {response.text}")
            raise ValueError(f"Provider returned invalid JSON. Status Code: {response.status_code}") from None
        response.raise_for_status()

        if "choices" not in response_json or not response_json["choices"]:
            error_detail = response_json.get("error", response_json)
            logger.warning(f"API returned 200 but no 'choices' in response: {error_detail}")
            raise ValueError(f"API response missing 'choices' key. Response: {error_detail}")

        return response_json["choices"][0]["message"]["content"]
    except requests.exceptions.HTTPError as e:
        // ... error message extraction logic ...
        raise Exception(error_message) from e
    except requests.exceptions.ConnectionError as e:
        raise Exception(f"Failed to connect to {provider} API. Check your network connection.") from e
    except requests.exceptions.Timeout as e:
        raise Exception(f"Request to {provider} API timed out.") from e
    except requests.exceptions.RequestException as e:
        raise Exception(f"An error occurred while making the request to {provider}: {e}") from e
    except ValueError as e:
        raise Exception(f"Failed to parse response as JSON from {provider}. The server might have returned an invalid response.") from e

This method implements rigorous defensive programming patterns against non-standard REST responses. When targeting reasoning models via OpenRouter or Ollama, it automatically adjusts the request temperature to 1.0 (as required by most reasoning parsers) and injects vendor-compliant parameters (reasoning.effort or think/reasoning_effort). It checks for empty choice arrays and HTTP 200 error payloads before extracting generated content.

docs.title: _call_llm_gemini()
docs.text:
Visibility: Private Signature: def _call_llm_gemini(prompt: str, thinking_level: str | None = None) -> str:

Description: Executes a generative content request against the Google Gemini API using the official google-genai SDK (google.genai.Client). It authenticates via Google Cloud Vertex AI if GEMINI_PROJECT_ID is set, or via direct API key if GEMINI_API_KEY is present. It configures model parameters, calculates thinking token budgets when requested, dispatches generation via client.models.generate_content, and filters the returned candidate parts to concatenate text-only segments.

Parameters: * prompt (str): Text prompt sent to Gemini. * thinking_level (str | None, optional): Budget level mapping for model thinking ("low" -> 1024, "medium" -> 4096, "high" -> 8192). Defaults to None.

Returns: * str: The concatenated text output from all text candidate parts.

Raises: * ValueError: If neither GEMINI_PROJECT_ID nor GEMINI_API_KEY are defined in the environment.

Implementation: 

def _call_llm_gemini(prompt: str, thinking_level: str | None = None) -> str:
    if os.getenv("GEMINI_PROJECT_ID"):
        client = genai.Client(vertexai=True, project=os.getenv("GEMINI_PROJECT_ID"), location=os.getenv("GEMINI_LOCATION", "us-central1"))
    elif os.getenv("GEMINI_API_KEY"):
        client = genai.Client(api_key=os.getenv("GEMINI_API_KEY"))
    else:
        raise ValueError("Either GEMINI_PROJECT_ID or GEMINI_API_KEY must be set in the environment")
    model = os.getenv("GEMINI_MODEL", "gemini-3.7-flash")

    kwargs = {"model": model, "contents": [prompt]}

    if thinking_level:
        # Map string levels to budgets for the installed SDK version
        budget_map = {"low": 1024, "medium": 4096, "high": 8192}
        budget = budget_map.get(thinking_level.lower(), 4096)
        thinking_config = types.ThinkingConfig(include_thoughts=True, thinking_budget=budget)
        kwargs["config"] = types.GenerateContentConfig(thinking_config=thinking_config)

    response = client.models.generate_content(**kwargs)

    # Extract only text parts to avoid "non-text parts: ['thought_signature']" warnings
    if response.candidates and response.candidates[0].content.parts:
        text_parts = [part.text for part in response.candidates[0].content.parts if part.text is not None]
        return "".join(text_parts)
    return ""

The function handles specific Gemini 2.0/3.0/3.7 response structures where reasoning candidates contain non-text components (such as thought_signature parts). By explicitly iterating over response.candidates[0].content.parts and selecting only non-null part.text entries, it prevents serialization warnings and runtime crashes.

docs.title: call_llm()
docs.text:
Visibility: Public Signature: def call_llm(prompt: str, use_cache: bool = True, thinking_level: str | None = None) -> str:

Description: The primary entry point for executing LLM queries across the entire codebase. It calculates prompt token metrics via utils.token_utils.count_tokens, checks the local disk cache, logs request parameters and prompts, delegates execution to either _call_llm_gemini or _call_llm_provider, writes fresh responses back to disk cache, and logs timing benchmarks.

Parameters: * prompt (str): The complete prompt string to evaluate. * use_cache (bool, optional): Whether to inspect and write to llm_cache.json. Defaults to True. * thinking_level (str | None, optional): Desired reasoning effort ("low", "medium", "high"). Defaults to None.

Returns: * str: The generated text response from the cache or provider.

Raises: * Exception: Propagates any underlying network, authentication, or parsing exceptions raised by _call_llm_gemini or _call_llm_provider.

Implementation & Actual In-Source Usage: 

def call_llm(prompt: str, use_cache: bool = True, thinking_level: str | None = None) -> str:
    import time

    from utils.token_utils import count_tokens

    provider = get_llm_provider()
    model = os.environ.get(f"{provider}_MODEL", os.environ.get("GEMINI_MODEL", "unknown"))
    prompt_tokens = count_tokens(prompt)

    logger.info(f"{'=' * 80}")
    logger.info(
        f"LLM CALL START | provider={provider} | model={model} | thinking={thinking_level} | cache={'enabled' if use_cache else 'disabled'} | prompt_tokens={prompt_tokens:,}"
    )
    logger.info(f"PROMPT:\n{prompt}")

    # Check cache if enabled
    if use_cache:
        cache = load_cache()
        if prompt in cache:
            cached_response = cache[prompt]
            logger.info(f"CACHE HIT | response_chars={len(cached_response):,}")
            logger.info(f"RESPONSE (cached):\n{cached_response}")
            logger.info("LLM CALL END | result=cache_hit")
            return cached_response

    # Make the actual LLM call
    start_time = time.time()
    logger.info(f"API CALL | sending request to {provider}...")

    if provider == "GEMINI":
        response_text = _call_llm_gemini(prompt, thinking_level=thinking_level)
    else:  # generic method using a URL that is OpenAI compatible API (Ollama, ...)
        response_text = _call_llm_provider(prompt, thinking_level=thinking_level)

    elapsed = time.time() - start_time
    logger.info(f"API CALL COMPLETE | elapsed={elapsed:.1f}s | response_chars={len(response_text):,}")
    logger.info(f"RESPONSE:\n{response_text}")

    # Update cache if enabled
    if use_cache:
        cache = load_cache()
        cache[prompt] = response_text
        save_cache(cache)
        logger.info("CACHE WRITE | saved response to cache")

    logger.info(f"LLM CALL END | result=success | elapsed={elapsed:.1f}s")
    return response_text


# Module Test / Self-Execution Example (from __main__)
if __name__ == "__main__":
    test_prompt = "Hello, how are you?"

    # First call - should hit the API
    print("Making call...")
    response1 = call_llm(test_prompt, use_cache=False)
    print(f"Response: {response1}")

call_llm serves as the central hub for model invocation. It uses dynamic import for utils.token_utils.count_tokens to minimize circular dependency issues during initialization. Every step—including cache lookups, prompt tokens, execution elapsed time, and output payloads—is recorded through logger to guarantee auditability across long-running document generation jobs.

docs.title: utils.crawl_github_files
docs.text:
Original File Path: utils/crawl_github_files.py

Technical documentation and internal engineering reference for utils/crawl_github_files.py. This module provides routines for fetching, filtering, and parsing source files from remote GitHub repositories. It supports both Git-over-SSH cloning into temporary directories and recursive querying through the GitHub REST API (supporting specific branches, commit SHAs, subdirectories, .gitignore parsing via pathspec, and inclusion/exclusion pattern filtering via fnmatch).

docs.title: Architectural Overview
docs.text:
The module handles two distinct remote ingestion pipelines depending on the target URL scheme: 1. SSH Git Clone Mode (git@ or .git): Clones the remote repository into a temporary directory using git.Repo.clone_from, parses local .gitignore rules, walks the local filesystem, validates file sizes, skips non-text binaries, and loads file contents into memory. 2. GitHub REST API Mode (https://github.com/...): Resolves owner, repository, commit/branch ref, and subdirectory paths via GitHub API endpoints (/repos/{owner}/{repo}/branches, /repos/{owner}/{repo}/git/trees/{tree}, and /repos/{owner}/{repo}/contents/{path}). Recursively traverses directories, evaluates .gitignore fetched from the API, handles rate limits (X-RateLimit-Reset), decodes base64-encoded blobs, and extracts file contents.
